restatements.text: Prohibits carrying a concealed handgun without a permit issued by the county sheriff.
Requires the sheriff to issue a permit to an applicant who is 21 or older, is legally allowed to possess a handgun, and has completed an eight-hour safety course.

evidence.quote: No person may carry a concealed handgun without a concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.
evidence.why: It expands government mandates and regulatory powers by requiring individuals to obtain a permit from the sheriff to carry a concealed handgun.

analysis.answer: Current law allows a person 21 or older who may lawfully possess a handgun to carry it concealed without a permit. The measure changes this by requiring a concealed carry permit issued by the county sheriff.
Direct costs include the administrative expense for county sheriffs to process permits.
County sheriffs bear the administrative burden of processing applications, which may be funded by taxpayers or future application fees.
County sheriffs will need to establish or expand administrative systems to process permits and verify eligibility.
It addresses the potential risk of unregulated individuals carrying concealed handguns by establishing a formal permitting process.
County sheriffs gain the administrative power to process and issue permits, though their discretion is limited by the "shall issue" language.

The effect of concealed carry permitting and training requirements on public safety and crime rates is disputed. Some researchers find that stricter permitting laws reduce violent crime and accidental shootings, while others find no significant effect or argue that permit requirements disarm law-abiding citizens and do not deter criminals.
Sheriffs' offices will incur administrative costs to review applications, verify ages, and background check eligibility.

The text does not specify an amendment threshold, sunset clause, or whether it is constitutional or statutory, meaning it could likely be amended or repealed through the normal legislative or initiative process.
The measure adds a requirement that applicants must complete an eight-hour safety course to obtain the newly required concealed carry permit.
Compliance costs for applicants include the tuition for an eight-hour safety course. Opportunity costs include the eight hours spent in the course.
Applicants bear the cost of the safety course and the time required. Safety course providers benefit from increased demand for their services.
Some individuals may choose not to carry a concealed handgun due to the time and cost of the safety course. Demand for certified firearm safety instructors will likely increase.
It addresses the potential risk of untrained individuals carrying concealed handguns by mandating a baseline level of training.
Firearm safety instructors gain influence and revenue as gatekeepers for the required training.

flags.note: The text does not specify what content the safety course must cover, who is authorized to teach it, or how sheriffs verify its completion.

flags.quote: The sheriff shall issue a permit
flags.note: The measure requires county sheriffs to process and issue permits without providing a funding mechanism or authorization for application fees to cover administrative costs.
